verdicts.killed_claim: The exact finite support-descent criterion is a new general theorem.
verdicts.retained_value: Application-specific finite quotient admissibility audit, explicit HOLD semantics, and fibrewise uncertainty bookkeeping.

verdicts.killed_claim: Identical admitted observations failing to identify hidden origin is a new theorem family.
verdicts.retained_value: Exteriority-specific forensic stopping rule and explicit reopening requirement.
verdicts.terminology_correction: Use target-informative auxiliary witness by default; reserve exogenous for separately demonstrated exogeneity.

verdicts.killed_claim: The component concepts are individually novel.
verdicts.retained_value: Explicit four-coordinate forensic separation plus temporal non-retroactivity as an accounting rule.
verdicts.terminology_correction: TD613 V should not rely on unqualified observability because standard control-theoretic observability aligns more closely with L.

verdicts.killed_claim: Receiver-specific non-equivalent views are themselves novel.
verdicts.retained_value: Receiver indexing combined with shared invariant custody/control, route memory, and authority non-transfer.
verdicts.terminology_correction: Anisotropic remains analogical unless directional structure/permeability is formally defined.

verdicts.retained_value: Exact ordered composition from capacity/coarsening through policy/admission and naming to registered event remains held for full-composition prior-art audit.

verdicts.killed_claim: Route history, authorization proof/revalidation, and replay are novel component concepts.
verdicts.retained_value: TD613 integration of route history, bounded authority, receiver projection and return revalidation; separately earned formal discrete holonomy remains independently scoped.
verdicts.terminology_correction: Reserve holonomy for the formal discrete transport result; describe the broader governance stack conventionally.

verdicts.killed_claim: Withdrawal or revocation as such is a TD613 novelty.
verdicts.retained_value: Reparative-validity criterion requiring useful handoff to remain functional after the custodian ceases participation.
verdicts.terminology_correction: Exit-preserving governance and post-participation portability are candidate explanatory phrases, not claimed standard terms.
